syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Challenges for the new nation-state
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges for the new nation-state; Three Challenges

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the circumstances in which India became independent and the two goals shared by the national movement.
Identify the three challenges of unity, democracy and development faced by independent India.

topics.title: Partition: the process
topics.ncert_sections: Partition: displacement and rehabilitation; Process of partition

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the two-nation theory and the opposition to it.
Analyse the difficulties in applying the principle of religious majorities to divide British India.

topics.title: Consequences of partition
topics.ncert_sections: Consequences of partition; Mahatma Gandhi's sacrifice

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the human, administrative and emotional consequences of partition.
Explain Mahatma Gandhi's efforts to restore communal harmony after partition.
Explain why India's leaders chose the ideal of a secular nation after partition.

topics.title: Integration of Princely States: the problem and the approach
topics.ncert_sections: Integration of Princely States; The problem; Government's approach

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the lapse of British paramountcy created the problem of the princely states.
Describe the government's approach, Sardar Patel's role and the Instrument of Accession.

topics.title: Hyderabad, Manipur and other difficult accessions
topics.ncert_sections: Hyderabad; Manipur

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the events that led to Hyderabad's accession to India.
Describe how Manipur and Junagadh became part of India.

topics.title: Reorganisation of States
topics.ncert_sections: Reorganisation of States

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the linguistic principle was promised, postponed and finally accepted.
Describe the Vishalandhra movement and the role of Potti Sriramulu.
State the work of the States Reorganisation Commission and evaluate the effects of linguistic states.

topics.title: Creation of new states
topics.ncert_sections: Fast Forward: Creation of new states

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the creation of states after 1956 such as Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab and the north-eastern states.
Explain the non-linguistic bases of later demands for new states.

topics.title: Challenge of building democracy
topics.ncert_sections: Challenge of building democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why India's leaders chose the democratic path and how they viewed the purpose of politics.
Describe how the Election Commission prepared for the first general election, including delimitation and electoral rolls.

topics.title: The first general election and changing methods of voting
topics.ncert_sections: Challenge of building democracy; Changing methods of voting

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate why the 1952 general election was a landmark in the history of democracy.
Trace the change from candidate-wise ballot boxes to stamped ballot papers and the EVM.

topics.title: Congress dominance in the first three general elections
topics.ncert_sections: Congress dominance in the first three general elections; Communist victory in Kerala

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the extent of Congress victories in the 1952, 1957 and 1962 elections.
Analyse how the first-past-the-post system magnified the Congress's seat share.
Describe the Communist victory in Kerala in 1957 and its dismissal in 1959.

topics.title: Nature of Congress dominance
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Congress dominance

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the Congress's dominance under democratic conditions from one-party rule elsewhere.
Explain the factors rooted in the freedom struggle that led to Congress dominance.

topics.title: Congress as social and ideological coalition; tolerance and management of factions
topics.ncert_sections: Congress as social and ideological coalition; Tolerance and management of factions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Congress became a broad social and ideological coalition.
Analyse how factionalism worked within the Congress and why the period is called the 'Congress system'.

topics.title: Emergence of opposition parties
topics.ncert_sections: Emergence of opposition parties; Socialist Party; Communist Party of India; Bharatiya Jana Sangh

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the leaders, ideologies and positions of the Socialist Party, the CPI and the Bharatiya Jana Sangh.
Evaluate the role opposition parties played in keeping the system democratic despite few seats.

topics.title: Political contestation over development
topics.ncert_sections: Political contestation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why major development choices must be political decisions taken or approved by the people's representatives.
Identify the competing interests of different groups in a development project such as mining in Orissa.

topics.title: Ideas of development
topics.ncert_sections: Ideas of development

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how development was equated with Western-style modernisation after Independence.
Distinguish the liberal-capitalist and socialist models of development available to India in 1947.
State what the terms Left and Right mean regarding the role of the state in the economy.

topics.title: Planning and the Planning Commission
topics.ncert_sections: Planning

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Planning Commission was set up, its advisory role and its objectives.
Explain the significance of the Bombay Plan of 1944 drafted by big industrialists.
Identify the world experiences that built public support for planning in the 1940s and 1950s.

topics.title: The early initiatives and the First Five Year Plan
topics.ncert_sections: The Early Initiatives; The First Five Year Plan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how five year plans and the plan and non-plan budgets worked, and why a plan holiday was taken in 1966.
Describe the agrarian focus of the First Five Year Plan and the idea of hastening slowly.
Explain why planners sought to raise savings in order to raise national income.

topics.title: Rapid industrialisation and the Second Plan
topics.ncert_sections: Rapid Industrialisation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Second Plan's stress on heavy industry and the public sector under P.C. Mahalanobis.
State the significance of the Avadi resolution on a socialist pattern of society.
Evaluate the problems and criticisms of the industry-first plan strategy.

topics.title: International context of India's foreign policy
topics.ncert_sections: International context; The Constitutional principles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the post-war world and India's own concerns shaped its early foreign policy.
Interpret Nehru's view that the conduct of foreign relations is the test of independence.
Identify the Directive Principles in Article 51 on promoting international peace and security.

topics.title: The policy of non-alignment and Nehru's role
topics.ncert_sections: The Policy of non-alignment; Nehru's role; Distance from two camps

concepts.learning_objective: State the objectives of Nehru's foreign policy and the domestic debate around it.
Analyse why India kept away from Cold War military blocs and how it balanced between them.

topics.title: Afro-Asian unity
topics.ncert_sections: Afro-Asian unity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain India's efforts for Asian unity, decolonisation and against racism.
Describe the significance of the Bandung Conference and the founding of the Non-Aligned Movement.

topics.title: Peace with China: Panchsheel and Tibet
topics.ncert_sections: Peace and conflict with China; Tibet

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the friendly start of India-China relations and the Panchsheel principles of 1954.
Explain how the Tibet question caused tension between India and China.

topics.title: The Chinese invasion, 1962
topics.ncert_sections: The Chinese invasion, 1962

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the India-China boundary dispute and the course of the 1962 war.
Evaluate the effects of the 1962 war on India's image, leadership and external ties.
Explain the war's effect on the Communist Party of India and on the Northeast.

topics.title: Wars and peace with Pakistan
topics.ncert_sections: Wars and Peace with Pakistan

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Kashmir conflict of 1947 and the cooperation that continued, including the Indus Waters Treaty.
Describe the course and outcome of the 1965 war and the Tashkent Agreement.

topics.title: Bangladesh war, 1971 and the cost of conflict
topics.ncert_sections: Bangladesh war, 1971

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the crisis in East Pakistan and the course and outcome of the 1971 war.
Analyse the US-China-Pakistan axis and the Indo-Soviet Treaty of 1971.
Explain how the wars with neighbours affected India's planning and defence spending.

topics.title: India's nuclear policy and shifting alliances
topics.ncert_sections: India's nuclear policy; Shifting alliances in world politics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain India's nuclear programme, its 1974 test and its stand on the NPT.
Describe the shifts in India's foreign policy after 1977 and after 1990.
Evaluate the broad consensus among Indian parties on foreign policy matters.

chapters.title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

topics.title: Challenge of political succession: from Nehru to Shastri to Indira Gandhi
topics.ncert_sections: Challenge of Political Succession; From Nehru to Shastri; From Shastri to Indira Gandhi

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the succession after Nehru raised doubts about India's democracy and how it was resolved.
Describe the challenges India faced during Lal Bahadur Shastri's Prime Ministership.
Explain how and why Indira Gandhi was chosen as Prime Minister in 1966.

topics.title: Fourth General Elections, 1967: context and non-Congressism
topics.ncert_sections: Fourth General Elections, 1967; Context of the elections; Non-Congressism

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the economic and social crisis that formed the background to the 1967 elections.
Explain the strategy of non-Congressism and Ram Manohar Lohia's argument for it.

topics.title: Electoral verdict of 1967, coalitions and defection
topics.ncert_sections: Electoral verdict; Coalitions; Defection

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the results of the 1967 elections at the national and State levels.
Explain the nature of the SVD coalition governments formed after 1967.
Explain the meaning of defection and the 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram' phenomenon.

topics.title: Split in the Congress: Indira Gandhi vs the Syndicate
topics.ncert_sections: Split in the Congress; Indira vs. the 'Syndicate'; Presidential election, 1969; Abolition of Privy Purse

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Syndicate and analyse how Indira Gandhi turned her power struggle with it into an ideological one.
Explain how the 1969 Presidential election led to the formal split of the Congress.
Explain what the privy purse was and how it came to be abolished.

topics.title: The 1971 election and restoration of Congress
topics.ncert_sections: The 1971 Election and Restoration of Congress; The contest; The outcome and after

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the composition and weakness of the Grand Alliance of 1971.
Explain the purpose of the 'Garibi Hatao' slogan in Indira Gandhi's political strategy.
Interpret the results of the 1971 Lok Sabha election and their consequences.

topics.title: Restoration? The nature of the new Congress
topics.ncert_sections: Restoration?

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the new Congress under Indira Gandhi with the old Congress system.
Analyse why democratic spaces shrank despite the consolidation of the Congress.

topics.title: Background to Emergency and the economic context
topics.ncert_sections: Background to Emergency; Economic context

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Bangladesh crisis, the stoppage of US aid, oil price rise, inflation and monsoon failure created discontent after 1971.
Describe the bitter party competition and the conflicting views of the Congress and the opposition about the judiciary and personal authority.

topics.title: Gujarat and Bihar movements and the Railway strike
topics.ncert_sections: Gujarat and Bihar movements; Railway Strike of 1974

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the causes, course and outcomes of the student agitations in Gujarat and Bihar in 1974-75.
Explain Jayaprakash Narayan's leadership of the Bihar movement and his call for total revolution.
Describe the 1974 Railway strike led by George Fernandes and the government's response to it.

topics.title: Conflict with the judiciary
topics.ncert_sections: Conflict with Judiciary

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the constitutional issues between Parliament and the Supreme Court that culminated in the Kesavananda Bharati case.
Evaluate the 1973 supersession of judges and the idea of a 'committed' judiciary and bureaucracy.

topics.title: Declaration of Emergency
topics.ncert_sections: Declaration of Emergency; Crisis and response

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Allahabad High Court verdict of 12 June 1975 and the Supreme Court's partial stay on it.
Explain how and on what grounds Emergency was proclaimed under Article 352 and what powers it gave the government.

topics.title: Consequences of the Emergency
topics.ncert_sections: Consequences

concepts.learning_objective: Describe press censorship, the bans on organisations and the acts of resistance during the Emergency.
Explain preventive detention and the significance of the April 1976 Supreme Court ruling on habeas corpus.
Identify the constitutional amendments made during the Emergency, including the forty-second amendment.

topics.title: Lessons of the Emergency
topics.ncert_sections: Lessons of the Emergency

concepts.learning_objective: Assess the strengths and weaknesses of Indian democracy that the Emergency revealed.
State the changes made to the Emergency provision after 1977, including armed rebellion and written Cabinet advice.
Analyse the unresolved issues of the balance between protest and governance and the politicisation of the police and administration.

topics.title: Politics after Emergency: the Lok Sabha elections of 1977
topics.ncert_sections: Politics after Emergency; Lok Sabha Elections, 1977

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Janata Party was formed and how it turned the 1977 election into a referendum on the Emergency.
Interpret the results of the 1977 Lok Sabha elections and their regional pattern.

topics.title: Janata Government and the legacy of the Emergency
topics.ncert_sections: Janata Government; Legacy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the factional struggle in the Janata government and the reasons for the mid-term elections of 1980.
Describe how non-Congressism and the politics of backward castes changed the party system after 1977.
Evaluate why the Emergency period is seen as both a constitutional and a more serious political crisis.

topics.title: Region and the nation: the Indian approach and areas of tension
topics.ncert_sections: Region and the Nation; Indian approach; Areas of tension

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Indian approach balances unity and diversity and treats regional aspirations democratically.
Identify the major regional tensions India faced in the first decades after Independence.

topics.title: Jammu and Kashmir
topics.ncert_sections: Jammu and Kashmir; Roots of the Problem; External and internal disputes; Politics since 1948; Insurgency and After; 2002 and Beyond

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the circumstances of Jammu and Kashmir's accession and the idea of Kashmiriyat.
Distinguish the opposite reactions to the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370.
Trace the political developments in Jammu and Kashmir from 1948 to 2019 and explain the rise of insurgency.

topics.title: The Dravidian movement
topics.ncert_sections: Dravidian movement (box)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the aims and democratic methods of the Dravidian movement and the DMK's early agitations.
Evaluate how Dravidian parties show the compatibility of regionalism and nationalism.

topics.title: Punjab
topics.ncert_sections: Punjab; Political context; Cycle of violence; Road to peace

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the political context of Akali politics and the Anandpur Sahib Resolution.
Describe Operation Blue Star, the assassination of Indira Gandhi and the anti-Sikh violence of 1984.
Identify the provisions of the Punjab Accord and analyse how peace returned to Punjab.

topics.title: The North-East: autonomy and secession
topics.ncert_sections: The North-East; Demands for autonomy; Secessionist movements

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the features of the North-East region and its political reorganisation.
Explain how autonomy demands in the North-East were accommodated within the constitutional framework.
Compare the secessionist movements in Mizoram and Nagaland and their outcomes.

topics.title: Movements against outsiders and the Assam Movement
topics.ncert_sections: Movements against outsiders

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why migration into the North-East led to movements against 'outsiders'.
Analyse the causes, methods and outcome of the Assam Movement and the Assam Accord of 1985.

topics.title: Accommodation and national integration
topics.ncert_sections: Accommodation and National Integration; Sikkim's merger (box); Goa's liberation (box)

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the lessons the chapter draws for accommodating regional aspirations in a democracy.
Describe how Sikkim and Goa became part of the Indian Union.

topics.title: Context of the 1990s
topics.ncert_sections: Context of the 1990s

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the five developments of the late 1980s that had a long-lasting impact on Indian politics.
Explain why the 1989 elections are said to mark the end of the 'Congress system'.

topics.title: Era of Coalitions
topics.ncert_sections: Era of Coalitions; Decline of Congress; Alliance politics

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the National Front government of 1989 was formed and supported.
Explain the emergence of a multi-party system and coalition governments at the Centre after 1989.
Analyse the shifting political equations behind the United Front and NDA governments.

topics.title: Political Rise of Other Backward Classes and the Mandal Commission
topics.ncert_sections: Political Rise of Other Backward Classes; 'Mandal' implemented; The Mandal Commission

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of the administrative category 'Other Backward Classes'.
Recall the setting up and main recommendations of the Mandal Commission.
Describe the implementation of the Mandal recommendation in 1990 and the Supreme Court's ruling on it.

topics.title: Political Fallouts: Dalit Politics and the BSP
topics.ncert_sections: Political fallouts

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the emergence of the Bahujan Samaj Party from BAMCEF under Kanshi Ram.
Explain the idea of Bahujan empowerment and the political success of the BSP.

topics.title: Communalism, Secularism, Democracy: Rise of the BJP and the Shah Bano Case
topics.ncert_sections: Communalism, Secularism, Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the formation of the BJP and its shift towards Hindutva and nationalism.
Explain the Shah Bano case and the political debate that followed the 1986 Act.

topics.title: Ayodhya Issue and its Resolution
topics.ncert_sections: Ayodhya Issue; From Legal Proceedings to Amicable Acceptance

concepts.learning_objective: Sequence the major events in the Ayodhya dispute from 1528 to 1992.
Explain the 2019 Supreme Court verdict and what it shows about resolving conflicts in a democracy.

topics.title: Lok Sabha Elections (2004-2019)
topics.ncert_sections: Lok Sabha Elections (2004-2019)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the formation and functioning of the Congress-led UPA governments of 2004 and 2009.
Interpret the results of the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections and party-position data.

topics.title: Growing Consensus
topics.ncert_sections: Growing consensus

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four elements of the consensus that has emerged among most political parties.
Evaluate how coalition politics and popular movements shape democratic politics within this consensus.
